9/13/2026
UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
09/14/2026
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Vv. Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD
The Honorable Judge

Rossie D. Alston Jr.

KATIE HALL, individually;

NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;

and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

Defendants.

MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF'S RULE 72(a)
OBJECTIONS TO ECF NOS. 63-65 AND MOTION TO SET ASIDE
ECF NO. 64, SUSPEND ENFORCEMENT AND DISCOVERY
BRIEFING, AND RESTORE ORAL ARGUMENT FOLLOWING
DETERMINATION OF ECF NO. 59

I. PRELIMINARY STATEMENT

Meta objected that Plaintiff's proposed supplemental pleading did not include the proposed
complaint in its entirety. ECF No. 53 at 3 n.1. Plaintiff responded with one complete proposed
Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint. ECF Nos. 59, 59-1. Plaintiff submitted a
declaration addressing his legal name and Meta-account usage. ECF No. 59-2. Plaintiff submitted
a memorandum identifying and locating the material amendments by category and section and

explaining their relationship to the existing claims. ECF No. 60. The motion identifies ECF No. 5

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 _ Filed 09/14/26 Page 2 of 26 PagelD# 698

as the pleading the proposed complaint would replace. ECF No. 59 4 3. Plaintiff did not concede
Meta's objection. ECF No. 59 4 1; ECF No. 60 at 4. Plaintiff removed it from the case.

ECF No. 64 states that the Court lacks sufficient information to decide the amendment
motion. ECF No. 64 requires an additional comparison against ECF No. 1 by September 11, 2026,
two calendar days after entry. Plaintiff receives court notices by mail. Plaintiff does not receive
electronic court notifications. Plaintiff obtained actual notice of the requirement at about 9:09 p.m.
on September 11, 2026. Ex. A 44 3-9.

The orders also changed the disposition of the pending discovery motions. ECF No. 62
withdrew ECF No. 26, vacated its hearing, and expressly preserved the other scheduled hearings.
ECF No. 63 terminated the hearing on ECF No. 15. ECF No. 65 terminated the hearing on ECF No.
94 and set opposition and reply deadlines while the amendment request remained unresolved.

Plaintiff challenges the additional condition on the record presented: the information
already supplied, the cumulative comparison selected, and the notice-and-performance interval
imposed. Plaintiff requests that ECF No. 64 be set aside and that ECF No. 59 proceed to
determination on the existing submissions and permitted briefing. Plaintiff requests briefing on the
discovery motions addressed to the resulting operative pleading, and oral argument on those
motions after that briefing.

Il. GOVERNING REVIEW AND TIMELINESS

A district judge "must consider timely objections and modify or set aside any part of the
order that is clearly erroneous or is contrary to law." Fed. R. Civ. P. 72(a); see 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)
(1)(A). A finding is clearly erroneous when the record leaves the reviewing court with a definite
and firm conviction that a mistake has been committed. An order is contrary to law when it applies

an incorrect legal standard or misapplies the governing rules. Local Civil Rule 72 provides that an

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 3 of 26 PagelD# 699

objection under Rule 72(a) "shall be considered a motion and is subject to the briefing and notice
requirements" of Local Civil Rule 7.

These objections address the stated premise of each order and the procedure each order
imposes. Part IV addresses the finding in ECF No. 64 that the Court lacked sufficient information.
Parts III and V address the deadline and the comparison baseline. Part VI addresses the sequence
ECF Nos. 63 and 65 set for the discovery motions. Part VII states the grounds for interim and
continuing case-management relief. Part VIII addresses oral argument. Part IX addresses the
Magistrate Judge's authority to impose the case-wide generative-artificial-intelligence provision
and, alternatively, its specification. Part X states the determinations sought.

The Court entered ECF Nos. 63 and 64 on September 9, 2026. The Court entered ECF No.
65 on September 10, 2026. The Court serves orders on Plaintiff by mail. Ex. A 4 3. Plaintiff
obtained actual notice of ECF Nos. 62 through 65 at about 9:09 p.m. on September 11, 2026. Ex. A
4 8. Plaintiff submitted these objections on September 13, 2026. Fourteen days from September 9 is
September 23. The objections are timely under Rule 72(a) without resort to Rule 6(d). The deadline
for objecting is distinct from the September 11 production date fixed by ECF No. 64. The first
governs this filing. Part II] addresses the second.

Rule 46 requires a party to state the action the party wants the court to take and the grounds
for the objection. Fed. R. Civ. P. 46. Each Part below identifies the ruling, the ground, and the
correction requested.

Il. THE SEPTEMBER 11 DEADLINE DID NOT AFFORD THE NOTICE-
AND-PERFORMANCE INTERVAL REQUIRED IN THESE
CIRCUMSTANCES

A. The chronology established by the declaration

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 4 of 26 PagelD# 700

Plaintiff proceeds pro se. Plaintiff is not a registered CM/ECF user and has not consented to
electronic service. Ex. A 43. Plaintiff receives no Notices of Electronic Filing. Ex. A 43. The Court
serves orders on Plaintiff by mail at his address of record, which is a commercial mail-receiving
agency. Ex. A ¥ 3.

Plaintiff supplements mail service with periodic docket review. At Plaintiff's direction, a
person acting on his behalf accesses PACER and uploads documents to the RECAP archive on
CourtListener. Ex. A q 4. Plaintiff maintains a CourtListener docket alert for this action. Ex. A ¥ 4.
In Plaintiff's experience, a CourtListener alert issues only when a document is added to the RECAP
archive for the docket. Ex. A 4 4. Plaintiff receives no other electronic notification of docket
activity. Ex. A ¥ 4.

Plaintiff's last submission before the orders at issue was the September 7, 2026 EDSS
submission docketed September 8 as ECF Nos. 57 through 61. Ex. A 95. From about September 7
through the afternoon of September 11, 2026, Plaintiff was unwell and did not work on this action.
Ex. A 46. At Plaintiff's direction, no docket review occurred during that period. Ex. A § 6. On the
evening of September 11, Plaintiff resumed work. Ex. A § 7. He understood the September 25,
2026 hearing to remain scheduled as to ECF Nos. 15 and 54. Ex. A 4 7. He intended to prepare for
that hearing and to decide whether to arrange travel pending a ruling on ECF No. 41. Ex. A 4 7.
Plaintiff requested that the docket be reviewed and any new documents uploaded. Ex. A 4 7.

At about 9:09 p.m. Eastern Time on September 11, Plaintiff received a CourtListener alert
for this action. Ex. A 4 8. Plaintiff then opened the CourtListener docket page for this action. That

was the first time Plaintiff learned of ECF Nos. 62, 63, 64, or 65. Ex. A JJ 8-9.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 5 of 26 PagelD# 701

As of the execution of the declaration, Plaintiff had not received a mailed copy of ECF No.
62, 63, 64, or 65 at his address of record. Ex. A J 10. The record does not show the date on which
the Clerk mailed the orders.

Entry of an order, service by mail, actual notice, and the opportunity to prepare a required
submission are different events. ECF No. 64 fixed the submission date without providing a period
measured from Plaintiff's receipt of notice.

B. The rules-based and due-process grounds

Formal service. Rule 77(d)(1) requires the Clerk to serve notice of entry of an order as
provided in Rule 5(b). Rule 5(b)(2)(C) provides that service by mail "is complete upon mailing.”
Fed. R. Civ. P. 5(b)(2)(C); Fed. R. Civ. P. 77(d)(1). Completion of service upon mailing fixes the
service date. It does not fix the date of receipt or the date of awareness. ECF No. 64 was entered
September 9. ECF No. 64 set September 11 as the performance date. No mailed copy had reached
Plaintiff by the time he executed his declaration. Ex. A ¥ 10.

Actual notice under Rule 83(b). A judge may regulate practice "in any manner consistent
with federal law, rules adopted under 28 U.S.C. §§ 2072 and 2075, and the district's local rules."
Fed. R. Civ. P. 83(b). The same rule provides: "No sanction or other disadvantage may be imposed
for noncompliance with any requirement not in federal law, federal rules, or the local rules unless
the alleged violator has been furnished in the particular case with actual notice of the requirement.”
Id. No federal rule requires a redlined comparison with a motion for leave to amend. No Local Civil
Rule of this Court requires one. The absence of a generally applicable redline requirement
identifies ECF No. 64 as a case-specific direction governed by Rule 83(b). Plaintiff obtained actual
notice of that direction at about 9:09 p.m. on the compliance date. Ex. A 8. That notice informed

him of an obligation already due that day.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 6 of 26 PagelD# 702

Opportunity to perform. Rule 83(b) addresses actual notice of a case-specific
requirement. The opportunity to act after notice is a related but distinct question. Notice must be
"reasonably calculated, under all the circumstances, to apprise interested parties" of the
requirement and "must afford a reasonable time for those interested to make their appearance."
Mullane v. Cent. Hanover Bank & Tr. Co., 339 U.S. 306, 314 (1950). Whether a party has had a
reasonable opportunity depends on the circumstances presented and the reasons offered. Ungar v.
Sarafite, 376 U.S. 575, 589-91 (1964). Plaintiff challenges both the two-calendar-day period fixed
when the order issued and the opportunity remaining after actual notice. Actual notice at the end of
the compliance date does not establish that Plaintiff had a reasonable opportunity to prepare,
verify, and submit the required comparison. The Court's Electronic Document Submission System
marks accepted documents as filed on the date of submission. E.D. Va., Electronic Document
Submission System (EDSS) User Manual 5 (Apr. 2026); see Ex. A § 11. Plaintiff's objection
concerns the time available to prepare and submit the comparison. The date of the Clerk's later
docketing is not the basis of that objection.

Plaintiff requested expedited determination of the materials already submitted, after
completion of briefing. ECF No. 59 § 14; ECF No. 60 at 15-16. That request sought prompt
adjudication of an existing submission. That request did not seek an expedited obligation to prepare
additional material.

C. The remedy

Plaintiff requests vacatur of ECF No. 64. Plaintiff requests an order that ECF No. 59 shall
not be denied, deemed abandoned, excluded from consideration, or otherwise disadvantaged based

on the absence of a comparison document on September 11, 2026.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 7 of 26 PagelD# 703

If the Court treats the September 11 date as a deadline that survives review, Plaintiff
requests an extension under Rule 6(b)(1)(B) for excusable neglect. The determination "is at bottom
an equitable one, taking account of all relevant circumstances," including "the danger of prejudice
to the [nonmovant], the length of the delay and its potential impact on judicial proceedings, the
reason for the delay, including whether it was within the reasonable control of the movant, and
whether the movant acted in good faith." Pioneer Inv. Servs. Co. v. Brunswick Assocs. Ltd. P'ship,
507 U.S. 380, 395 (1993). The Fourth Circuit treats the reason for the delay as the most important
factor. Thompson v. E.I. DuPont de Nemours & Co., 76 F.3d 530, 533-34 (4th Cir. 1996).

Each factor is addressed on this record. Prejudice: no response to ECF No. 59 was yet due
on September 11, no Defendant had asserted that the submission was insufficient, and no order or
filing identifies harm from the absence of a comparison document. Length and impact: Plaintiff
sought relief on the first business day after actual notice. He requests suspension during review
and, if a comparison requirement is sustained, seven calendar days after actual notice of that
determination to comply. No response to ECF No. 59 was yet due on September 11. Plaintiff
requests no suspension of briefing on ECF No. 59. The requested pause concerns enforcement of
the comparison requirement and the specified discovery proceedings. Reason and control: Plaintiff
did not know the obligation existed until about 9:09 p.m. on the compliance date, and Plaintiff was
unwell from about September 7 through the afternoon of September 11. Ex. A §{{ 6, 8. Thompson
involved a party who knew the deadline and entrusted the filing to outgoing mail. 76 F.3d at 532—
34. This record involves a newly created obligation of which Plaintiff first learned at
approximately 9:09 p.m. on the compliance date, without a meaningful remaining opportunity to

perform. The two situations are distinct. Good faith: Plaintiff sought review on the first business

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 8 of 26 PagelD# 704

day after notice, disclosed the chronology under penalty of perjury, and committed to produce any
comparison the District Judge sustains within seven days of actual notice of that ruling.

Rule 6(d) does not supply this relief. Rule 6(d) adds three days to a period that runs from
service by mail. ECF No. 64 fixed a calendar date. Rule 6(d) does not move a fixed calendar date.

IV. THE INFORMATION-SUFFICIENCY DETERMINATION MUST BE
ASSESSED AGAINST ECF NOS. 59 AND 60

A. The procedural objection Plaintiff addressed

Meta's opposition to ECF No. 26 objected that Plaintiff attached "only his supplemental
allegations, 'incorporating by reference’ the remainder of his FAC," rather than "a copy of the
proposed amended pleading in its entirety." ECF No. 53 at 3 n.1. Plaintiff answered that objection
five days later. ECF No. 59 at 1-3; ECF No. 60 at 1-4. The asserted absence of a complete
proposed pleading was the subject of Meta's form objection. ECF No. 59 supplied that pleading.
ECF No. 60 explained the form of the submission and the substance of the proposed changes.
Plaintiff did not concede that ECF No. 26 was defective. ECF No. 59 4 1; ECF No. 60 at 4.

B. What the existing submission supplied

ECF No. 64 states that the Court lacked "sufficient information to issue an Order." The

submission before the Court on September 9 contained the following.

Record location Information available to the Court on September 9, 2026
ECF No. 59 §§ 3-5 ECF No. 5 identified as the operative pleading. The proposed
replacement identified. The same parties, six counts, and
categories of relief retained. Four categories of additional facts,
each cited to a section of the proposed pleading.

ECF No. 59 §q 7-13 Relationship of the motion to ECF Nos. 26 and 43. Procedural
posture. No answer, no scheduling order, no Rule 26(f) conference,
no discovery.

ECF No. 60 at 1-4 The five principal changes. The integrated form. The governing
standards under Rules 15(a)(2) and 15(d). The response to Meta's
form objection.

ECF No. 60 at 5—7 Timing, procedural stage, and absence of prejudice under Laber.
ECF No. 60 at 7-10 Section-by-section description of the material amendments:

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 9 of 26 PagelD# 705

source-level falsity, search identifiers versus report contents,
subsequent events, retained counts.

ECF No. 60 at 10-15 Absence of bad faith. Futility analysis under the Rule 12(b)(6)
standard. Rule 15(d) supplementation. Procedural effect of
granting leave.

ECF No. 60 at 15-16 The requested sequence: expedited determination after Local Civil
Rule 7(F)(1) briefing.

ECF No. 59-2 4] 2-10; The declaration concerning Plaintiff's legal name and Meta-

ECF No. 59-1 8 S account usage, and the corresponding pleaded facts.
ECF No. 5; ECF No. 1 The operative pleading and the original pleading, both on the
docket.

ECF No. 60 is a twenty-page filing. Pages 1 through 16 are the memorandum. Pages 17
through 20 are the certificate of service and the Local Civil Rule 83.1(N) certification. The
memorandum identifies the material amendments by category. The memorandum locates each
category in the proposed pleading by section. The memorandum states the governing standard for
each. The complete proposed pleading was attached as ECF No. 59-1 and again as ECF No. 60-1.
ECF No. 5 was on the docket. ECF No. 1 was on the docket.

C. The objection to the additional condition

A redline may assist comparison. Plaintiff does not challenge the authority of a court to
request one. Plaintiff objects to the condition imposed on this record. ECF No. 64 made
consideration of ECF No. 59 contingent on an additional submission due September 11. The
complete proposed pleading and the explanation in ECF No. 60 were already before the Court.

ECF No. 64 identifies the comparison it requires. On the record presented, ECF No. 64 does
not connect the additional comparison, the selected baseline, and the September 11 deadline to an
informational need that ECF No. 60 left unmet. Plaintiff does not contend that Rule 52 or Rule 72
required ECF No. 64 to state findings; Rule 52(a)(3) generally does not require findings on a
motion. Plaintiff contends that the premise the order states is not supported by the record it

addresses. ECF No. 64 issued one day after ECF Nos. 59 and 60 were docketed. No Defendant's

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 _ Filed 09/14/26 Page 10 of 26 PagelD#
706

response was due under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1). No Defendant had asserted that the submission
was insufficient.

Rule 83(b) permits a judge to regulate practice in a manner consistent with federal law, the
federal rules, and the local rules. Fed. R. Civ. P. 83(b). A district court's inherent authority to
manage its docket "must be a 'reasonable response to the problems and needs’ confronting the
court's fair administration of justice." Dietz v. Bouldin, 579 U.S. 40, 45 (2016) (citation omitted).
The exercise "cannot be contrary to any express grant of or limitation on the district court's power
contained in a rule or statute." Id.; see id. at 45-48. ECF No. 64 identifies one problem: insufficient
information. The record on September 9 contained the complete proposed pleading, the pleading it
replaces, the original pleading, a sixteen-page memorandum identifying and locating the material
amendments, and a declaration. The condition imposed was a two-day requirement to produce a
cumulative comparison against a pleading the motion does not seek to replace. That condition does
not respond to the problem stated. Plaintiff requests review of the additional condition in light of
that record, the selected comparator, and the notice-and-performance interval.

Rule 15(a)(2) directs that the court "should freely give leave when justice so requires." Fed.
R. Civ. P. 15(a)(2). The Supreme Court has identified the grounds on which leave is denied: undue
delay, bad faith, dilatory motive, repeated failure to cure, undue prejudice, and futility. Foman v.
Davis, 371 U.S. 178, 182 (1962); Laber v. Harvey, 438 F.3d 404, 426-27 (4th Cir. 2006) (en banc).
The absence of a comparison document does not itself establish futility, prejudice, or bad faith. To
the extent nonperformance by September 11 is proposed as a procedural basis for denying
consideration of ECF No. 59, the validity of the condition and Plaintiff's opportunity to satisfy it
require separate determination. Plaintiff requests that the Rule 15 merits and the asserted

September 11 default be addressed separately.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 _ Filed 09/14/26 Page 11 of 26 PagelD#
707

Any proposed claim-terminating consequence based on September 11 nonperformance
would require separate consideration of the circumstances of that nonperformance, the notice and
warning provided, and the availability of less severe alternatives. Ballard v. Carlson, 882 F.2d 93,
95-96 (4th Cir. 1989) (dismissal); Hathcock v. Navistar Int'l Transp. Corp., 53 F.3d 36, 40—41 (4th
Cir. 1995) (default judgment). ECF No. 64 is not a sanctions order and contains no warning.
Plaintiff cites those authorities only against a consequence that would operate as a case-dispositive
sanction.

Plaintiff requests that the information-sufficiency finding be set aside. Plaintiff requests
that ECF No. 59 proceed to determination on the existing submission.

V. ECF NO. 64 USES A DIFFERENT BASELINE FROM THE PLEADING
ECF NO. 59 SEEKS TO REPLACE
ECF No. 59 seeks to replace ECF No. 5. ECF No. 59 43; ECF No. 60 at 2, 15. ECF No. 64

requires comparison to ECF No. 1. The ordered comparison therefore combines changes already
made through the First Amended Complaint with the changes presently proposed through ECF No.
59.

An amended pleading supersedes the original as the operative pleading and renders the
original of no legal effect. Young v. City of Mount Ranier, 238 F.3d 567, 572—73 (4th Cir. 2001).
Plaintiff filed ECF No. 5 as of right on August 6, 2026. ECF No. 59 § 10. Every pending motion to
dismiss is directed to ECF No. 5. ECF Nos. 10, 21, 45. ECF No. 1 may supply historical context. It
does not supply the baseline that isolates the amendments presently proposed. ECF No. 59 presents
two questions: whether the proposed pleading should replace ECF No. 5 under Rule 15(a)(2), and
whether the post-August 6 events should be added under Rule 15(d). Comparing the proposed
pleading to ECF No. 1 combines amendments already made with amendments now requested. ECF

No. 64 does not identify why that cumulative comparison was necessary in addition to the proposed

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 _ Filed 09/14/26 Page 12 of 26 PagelD#
708

pleading and ECF No. 60's explanation of the current amendments. This is Plaintiff's first motion
for leave to amend. No prior amendment was allowed by leave. ECF No. 60 at 10.

Plaintiff requests vacatur of the ECF No. 1 comparison requirement as part of the principal
relief.

Alternative relief. If the District Judge sustains a comparison requirement, Plaintiff
requests an order identifying the required baseline. Plaintiff requests seven calendar days after
actual notice of that determination to produce it. Plaintiff requests express relief from the
September 11, 2026 date. The package submits neither comparison. It seeks a ruling on the
requirement and a prospective period if the requirement survives review.

VI. THE AMENDMENT REQUEST SHOULD BE DETERMINED BEFORE
DISCOVERY BRIEFING IS COMPLETED AGAINST THE PLEADING IT
WOULD REPLACE

A. Plaintiff maintains all three substantive positions

Plaintiff maintains that the First Amended Complaint states each of its six claims and
survives the pending motions to dismiss. ECF Nos. 20, 30, 51. Plaintiff maintains that amendment
is warranted under Rule 15(a)(2) for the reasons stated in ECF No. 60 at 4-14. Plaintiff maintains
that the post-August 6 events independently warrant supplementation under Rule 15(d) for the
reasons stated in ECF No. 60 at 14-15. The standards governing amendment and supplementation
"are nearly identical," and leave under either "should be freely granted." Franks v. Ross, 313 F.3d
184, 198 n.15 (4th Cir. 2002). Plaintiff renews the request for leave through ECF No. 59. Plaintiff
incorporates ECF No. 60 at 2-16 by reference. Foman, 371 U.S. at 182; Laber, 438 F.3d at 426-29.

Vacating ECF No. 64 removes the disputed condition. Granting ECF No. 59 is the separate

action that makes the proposed pleading operative. Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a)(2), (d). Plaintiff requests

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 13 of 26 PagelD#
709

both. Vacatur alone preserves consideration of ECF No. 59. It does not make the proposed pleading
operative.

B. The consequence of the existing sequence

ECF No. 60 requested prompt determination so the parties could address one complete
operative pleading. ECF No. 64 imposed another submission requirement before determination of
that request. ECF No. 65 established discovery briefing while the request remained unresolved.
Plaintiff seeks a sequence in which the pleading determination precedes completion of briefing on
the discovery directed to those allegations.

ECF No. 54 remains supported by the operative First Amended Complaint and the existing
record. ECF No. 15 does as well. The First Amended Complaint pleads the three identifiers, the
letters’ wording, and the distinction between the letters and the source records. The proposed
pleading adds allegations bearing on the same requested discovery. Section S of the proposed
pleading alleges, on Plaintiff's personal knowledge, that Plaintiff never used "Marvelle J.
Ballentine" to create, register, identify, maintain, access, or operate any Meta account. ECF No. 59-
1 § S; ECF No. 59-2 4 2-10; ECF No. 60 at 7. Section S alleges, on information and belief, that
neither report as originally received by NCMEC contained or otherwise identified Plaintiff by that
name and that neither concerned Plaintiff personally. ECF No. 59-1 § S; ECF No. 60 at 7-8.
Section O adds NCMEC's August 12, 2026 statements and counsel's August 13, 2026 response.
ECF No. 59-1 § O; ECF No. 60 at 9.

The interrogatories are directed to those propositions. ECF No. 15 proposes three
interrogatories to NCMEC, each answerable "Yes," "No," or "Unable to determine after reasonable
inquiry," asking whether either report, as originally received by NCMEC, contained or otherwise

identified "Marvelle J. Ballentine," "Jay Ballentine," or jaychizza@icloud.com. ECF No. 15-1.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 14 of 26 PagelD#
710

ECF No. 54 proposes four interrogatories to Meta in the same form. ECF No. 54-1. The first asks
whether Meta submitted a CyberTipline report to NCMEC in connection with the Facebook
account terminated on or about July 4, 2022. Id. The remaining three ask whether any such report
contained any of the same three identifiers. Id. NCMEC's memorandum states that Plaintiff "does
not have access to those reports." ECF No. 11 at 9. The proposed pleading pleads what Plaintiff
knows and what Plaintiff alleges on information and belief as separate propositions. The
interrogatories are directed to the second category.

Briefing completed before determination of ECF No. 59 may require supplementation to
address the allegations subsequently made operative. Resolving ECF No. 59 first would permit one
round of briefing against the resulting operative pleading. Rule 15 governs when the proposed
pleading becomes operative. Rule 26 governs the discovery sought. Plaintiff does not contend that
the proposed pleading governs the action now. Plaintiff identifies its contents as the reason to
sequence the pleading determination before the discovery briefing.

C. Replacement schedule

Plaintiff requests suspension of the opposition and reply deadlines established by ECF No.
65 pending determination of ECF No. 59, followed by a replacement schedule addressed to the
resulting operative pleading. Plaintiff separately requests that determination of ECF Nos. 15 and 54
remain in abeyance until ECF No. 59 has been determined and the resulting court-authorized
briefing periods have concluded. ECF No. 15 is fully briefed. Its existing submissions should be
preserved, with any additional briefing limited to a material effect of the pleading determination.
ECF No. 54 has outstanding response and reply deadlines. Those deadlines should be replaced on

the triggering events stated below.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 _ Filed 09/14/26 Page 15 of 26 PagelD#
711

Plaintiff requests the ordinary intervals of Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1): fourteen days for the
response and six days for the reply. If ECF No. 59 is granted, service of the order granting leave and
deeming the Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint filed would start Meta's fourteen days
on ECF No. 54. If ECF No. 59 is denied, service of the order denying leave would start Meta's
fourteen days, with briefing addressed to the First Amended Complaint. If ECF No. 59 is granted in
part, the filing of the conforming pleading the order directs, within seven calendar days after
Plaintiff receives actual notice of the order directing that filing, would start Meta's fourteen days.
Because ECF No. 59 is not stayed and may be determined while these objections are pending, each
replacement response period and each initial supplemental-brief period should run from the later of
service of the order resolving these objections on the party required to act or the otherwise
applicable triggering event. Service of Meta's response would start Plaintiff's six days in each
branch. Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) supplies those intervals and permits a different court-ordered
arrangement. Each replacement date is defined by a future event so that the schedule operates
whenever the ruling issues.

ECF Nos. 15 and 54 should remain pending without withdrawal or refiling. The existing
briefing on ECF No. 15 (ECF Nos. 16, 31, 33, 36, 46, 52) should be preserved. The parties should
be permitted limited supplemental briefing on ECF No. 15 addressed to any material effect of the
pleading determination, on the same triggering events.

Alternative. If the Court permits Meta's briefing under ECF No. 65 to proceed, Plaintiff
separately requests that determination of ECF Nos. 15 and 54 be held in abeyance pending
determination of ECF No. 59. Upon any grant of ECF No. 59 in full or in part, Plaintiff requests
leave to submit supplemental briefing addressed to the resulting operative pleading before either

discovery motion is determined. The existing submissions on both motions should be preserved. A

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 Filed 09/14/26 Page 16 of 26 PagelD#
712

ruling that permits Meta's briefing to continue does not dispose of the separate request to defer
adjudication of both motions.

D. Determination of ECF No. 59 before or within any claim-terminating

disposition

Three motions to dismiss directed to the First Amended Complaint are pending before the
District Judge. ECF Nos. 10, 21, 45. ECF No. 59 is pending before the Magistrate Judge. A
disposition of the motions to dismiss that terminated a claim while ECF No. 59 remained
undetermined would decide the sufficiency of a pleading Plaintiff has moved to replace. It would
do so without addressing the motion to replace it. Plaintiff requests that ECF No. 59 be determined
before, or expressly within, any disposition of ECF Nos. 10, 21, or 45 that would terminate any
claim. To the extent a ruling on ECF No. 59 would foreclose a claim, Plaintiff requests that the
ruling issue in a form permitting the review 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1) provides for dispositive matters.

VII. GROUNDS FOR INTERIM AND CONTINUING CASE-MANAGEMENT
RELIEF

IX. THE CASE-WIDE CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENT MUST REST ON
THE MAGISTRATE JUDGE'S DELEGATED AUTHORITY

ECF No. 63 at 1 and ECF No. 65 at 1 each provide: "should any party utilize generative
artificial intelligence for the preparation of any filing submitted to this Court, that party must
identify the use of the generative artificial intelligence in the filing as well as provide a certification
that said party has reviewed all citations for accuracy."

ECF Nos. 63 and 65 require disclosure and certification for "any filing submitted to this
Court" when generative artificial intelligence is used in its preparation. The requirement applies
throughout this action. It reaches filings concerning matters before the District Judge, including
these objections. The language contains no limitation to filings concerning matters assigned to the
Magistrate Judge.

A magistrate judge exercises authority conferred by 28 U.S.C. § 636 and assigned by the

district court. Section 636(b)(1)(A) permits determination of assigned nondispositive pretrial

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 68 _ Filed 09/14/26 Page 22 of 26 PagelD#
718

matters. Section 636(b)(3) permits assignment of additional duties consistent with the Constitution
and federal law. Local Civil Rule 72 authorizes duties permitted by governing law and provides for
assignment or referral by an order entered in the action or instructions of a district judge.

Rule 83(b) permits procedural directions consistent with federal law. It does not
independently enlarge the duties assigned under § 636. The Fourth Circuit has identified § 636 as
the source of a magistrate judge's authority and has distinguished that statutory authority from the
inherent Article III powers of a district court. Reddick v. White, No. 08-2286, slip op. at 5—7 (4th
Cir. Dec. 1, 2011) (per curiam) (unpublished). Authority to administer an assigned matter does not,
by itself, establish authority to impose a continuing requirement on every filing in the action.

Plaintiff requests determination of the assignment governing the Magistrate Judge's
authority in this action and whether that assignment supports the requirement's case-wide reach.
Plaintiff requests that the provisions be confined to filings concerning matters assigned to the
Magistrate Judge and that their application to filings concerning matters retained by the District
Judge be set aside. Plaintiff requests a determination of authority before approval of a compliance
method.
